answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable deposit to a vertex before it can submit work; the protocol randomly selects deposited agents for costly audits, and a proven duplicate identity forfeits its bond. A quill can record the audit result, while a nebula of pseudonyms gains no extra influence unless each one funds a separate deposit. Sybil creation is therefore possible, but the attacker must immobilize real capital for every identity and risks losing it when duplicates are exposed.
